plan: Controls for the stage 4 blind review of issue #1009 (lane c-review-1009-1117)
written: before any program of this lane read a certificate; hashed with the checker at the freeze
applies_to: each of the thirteen counts 147, 156, 180, 210, 260, 262, 268, 270, 272, 292, 295, 299 and 307; the same 37 controls at each

terms.certificate: the two files of one count: form P, certificates/0000-0999/nN.cert (rows x y t), and form C, witnesses/2026-11-16/n-N.yaml (four corners)
terms.facts: the certificate's rows and side S as form P states them, and method A's exact margin of every pair and clearance of every square at every wall on the original files
terms.least step: 1/10^40, written e; 'past' a contact means e beyond it
terms.contact: a margin or a clearance of exactly 0
terms.decided: a changed packing is written as the bytes of both forms and read back through the readers; method A decides the form P rows and method B the form C corners, every square and every wall; the two files must be one packing square by square (the twin relation)
terms.pairs decided: a control that moves every square (G4 to G8, E1, K1, X1's mirrored packing, a W1 fallback) decides every pair again by both methods. A control that changes one square (G1, G2, P1, W1) decides again the n - 1 pairs that hold it, and a control that changes only the side or its spelling (R2, S1) decides no pair again; for every square such a control does not change it checks that the row and the corners read back are the original's. A pair's decision is a function of its two squares alone, so a pair not decided again has the original's decision. The receipts print such a decision's verdict as PARTIAL where this plan says accepted
terms.as stated: the verdict, the classes and every exact value named in the rule are those the rule gives, and the two methods agree at every wall and every pair decided; a decision in which they disagree fails its control
terms.original verdict: ACCEPT when both files are read, the twin relation holds at every square, no pair overlaps, no square crosses a wall, and the methods agree; the rules below are written for an accepted original, and name what changes otherwise where it is simple to

priors: P1. Every certificate is accepted, in both forms, with the twin relation at every square, every pair strictly apart and every wall strictly clear (the issue states least wall clearances of 1e-28 and least pair margins of 2e-28 or more).
P2. Each claim of the issue is the 12-place ceiling of its certificate's side.
P3. S1a is accepted at every count, and S1b wherever 1/q is at most the least right-or-top clearance.
P4. S1e is accepted and S1f refused at every count.
P5. K1c finds each certificate's first contact under uniform contraction within 1e-26 of scale 1: the certificates carry almost no padding.
P6. X1's mirrored packing is refused wherever a square is tilted.

controls.change: none: every pair's margin recomputed from the form C corners by projecting the eight corners on the four edge directions, and every clearance from the form P row by centre and half-extent in Fractions
controls.stated: equal to method A's margin at every pair and to its clearance at every square and wall

controls.change: the last square deleted from the original bytes with the count left as stated: the last line of form P and, apart, the last ten lines of form C
controls.stated: the reader of the changed form refuses: n stated, n - 1 listed; the other form is read

controls.change: the side written as 2p/2q in both forms
controls.stated: read; the side's value and every clearance equal to the original's, every row and corner the original's; accepted; only the side flagged non-canonical, in each form

controls.change: in form C the ids of squares 1 and 2 exchanged; apart, in form P rows 1 and 2 exchanged
controls.stated: form C: the reader refuses, ids out of order. Form P: read, and refused because the twin relation fails at exactly squares 1 and 2 and for no other reason; the rows read back are the original's with rows 1 and 2 exchanged

controls.change: the side written as a 40-place decimal: in form P, in form C as a quoted string, and in form C unquoted
controls.stated: refused by the reader each time: not a scalar p or p/q in form P and in the quoted form C, a YAML float in the unquoted form C

controls.change: a leading plus sign on the first coordinate of square 1 in the original bytes, in form P and, apart, in form C
controls.stated: the reader of the changed form refuses, naming that coordinate as not a scalar; the other form is read

controls.change: square n given square 1's row, in both forms
controls.stated: refused; the margins of the n - 1 pairs with square n exactly predicted: (1, n) is -1 and each (k, n) is the original (1, k); the overlapping pairs among them exactly (1, n) and any the prediction makes negative; method B's overlap area exactly 1 when (1, n) is the only one; square n's clearances are square 1's; every other square unchanged

controls.change: square 1 translated by (S, 0), in both forms
controls.stated: refused; square 1's clearances exactly (L + S, B, R - S, T), so it crosses the right wall; its area inside the box is 0 exactly when L >= 0; no pair with square 1 overlaps; every other square unchanged

controls.change: in form C, the first corner of square 1 moved by e in x
controls.stated: refused: square 1, and only square 1, is not a unit square by method B; no pose can be taken from its corners; the twin relation fails at square 1 only; method A's poses, from form P, are all unit

controls.change: in form C, every square listed in reverse
controls.stated: the original's verdict, with method A on the poses taken from the changed form C and method B on its corners: every margin and clearance identical to the original's; method B's classes identical; every sense exchanged; the twin relation holds

controls.change: in form C, every square listed from its second corner
controls.stated: as G4, with every sense unchanged

controls.change: every row transposed: (x, y, t) to (y, x, (1 - t)/(1 + t)), in both forms
controls.stated: the original's verdict; every margin identical; every square's clearances (L, B, R, T) become (B, L, T, R)

controls.change: a quarter turn about the box centre: (x, y, t) to (S - y, x, t), in both forms
controls.stated: the original's verdict; every margin identical; every square's clearances (L, B, R, T) become (T, L, B, R)

controls.change: mirrored: (x, y, t) to (S - x, y, -t), in both forms
controls.stated: the original's verdict; every margin identical; every square's clearances (L, B, R, T) become (R, B, L, T)

controls.change: the side lowered by e, in both forms
controls.stated: the side rule: every right and top clearance lowered by exactly the amount, every left and bottom clearance unchanged, every row and corner the original's; the contacts exactly the square-wall pairs whose new clearance is 0 and the crossings exactly those whose new clearance is negative; accepted exactly when nothing crosses

controls.change: the side lowered by 1/q, q the denominator of the side in lowest terms
controls.stated: the side rule

controls.change: the side lowered by W, the least clearance of any square at the right or top wall
controls.stated: the side rule; accepted, with contacts at the right or top exactly at the squares that attain W (the touching-wall branch: the box at the packing's upper extent)

controls.change: the side lowered by W + e
controls.stated: the side rule; refused, the crossings including every square that attains W

controls.change: the side set to the issue's claim
controls.stated: the side rule with the amount S less the claim (negative when the claim is above S)

controls.change: the side set to the issue's claim less 1e-12
controls.stated: the side rule with the amount S less the claim plus 1e-12

controls.change: every square translated by (-L*, -B*), the least left and bottom clearances, and the side set to X, the larger of the width S - L* - R* and the height S - B* - T*, R* and T* the least right and top clearances
controls.stated: the extent rule: every clearance exactly predicted, every margin identical; accepted; the left wall touched exactly by the squares that attain L*, the bottom by those that attain B*, and the right (when the width is the larger) or the top (when the height is) by those that attain R* or T*; nothing crosses. So X is the packing's extent and S - X its slack at the walls

controls.change: the same translation with the side X - e
controls.stated: the extent rule; refused; the crossings exactly the squares within e of the wall or walls of the larger extent

controls.change: the packing contracted uniformly about the origin to its first contact: every centre and the side multiplied by g*, the greatest over all pairs of H/max|d.w| and over all squares and walls of h/(distance from the centre to the wall), tilts unchanged
controls.stated: accepted; the touching pairs exactly those whose own factor equals g*, the wall contacts exactly the square-wall pairs whose factor equals g*, at least one of either; no pair overlaps and nothing crosses

controls.change: the same with the factor g*(1 - e)
controls.stated: refused; the overlapping pairs exactly those whose own factor exceeds g*(1 - e), the crossings exactly the square-wall pairs whose factor does

controls.change: one pair closed to exact contact, in both forms: the first pair in the order (margin, i, j), trying the second square moved toward the first and then the first toward the second, for which the moved square, at contact and at e past it, keeps every other margin and every clearance positive (the first 400 pairs are tried; if none is eligible, the first pair with its second square moved)
controls.stated: the pair's margin exactly 0, touching by both methods; the moved square's other margins and its clearances as the closed form gives them; every other square unchanged. With an eligible pair: accepted, and the only contact among the moved square's pairs is that pair

controls.change: the same pair closed to e past contact
controls.stated: the pair's margin exactly -e; refused; every other square unchanged. With an eligible pair: the only overlap among the moved square's pairs is that pair

controls.change: one square moved to the left wall, in both forms: the nearest square (least clearance, then least index) among the 60 nearest that keeps every margin positive at the wall and at e past it; if none is eligible, the whole packing translated to the wall
controls.stated: that square's clearance at the wall exactly 0 and at the opposite wall raised by the move, its other clearances and every other square unchanged, none of its pairs touching or overlapping; accepted; the only new wall contact is that square's. Fallback: every clearance exactly predicted, every margin identical, contact exactly at the squares of least clearance

controls.change: the same square moved e further
controls.stated: refused; that square's clearance exactly -e; the only new crossing is that square at that wall, and its area inside the box is below 1. Fallback: the crossings exactly the squares of least clearance

controls.change: as W1c-left, at the bottom wall
controls.stated: as W1c-left

controls.change: as W1p-left, at the bottom wall
controls.stated: as W1p-left

controls.change: as W1c-left, at the right wall
controls.stated: as W1c-left

controls.change: as W1p-left, at the right wall
controls.stated: as W1p-left

controls.change: as W1c-left, at the top wall
controls.stated: as W1c-left

controls.change: as W1p-left, at the top wall
controls.stated: as W1p-left

controls.change: every square, alone, moved perpendicular to its nearest wall (least clearance; ties in the order left, bottom, right, top) to contact and to e past it
controls.stated: method A's clearance and the closed form's exactly 0 and exactly -e; method B touching and crossing; method B's area inside the box exactly 1 at contact and below 1 past it

controls.change: every pair, alone, closed along its line of centres (the second square moved, the squares taken from form P) to contact and to e past it
controls.stated: method A's margin exactly 0 and exactly -e; the corner projections' margin exactly 0 at contact; method B touching and overlapping with positive area, its two clipping orders agreeing

controls.change: form P with every t replaced by -t (the tangent read clockwise), against the original form C; and the mirrored rows written in both forms and decided
controls.stated: the twin relation fails at exactly the squares whose t is not 0, 1 or -1, so the files are refused wherever a square is tilted; on the mirrored packing the two methods agree at every wall and pair (its verdict is recorded, not stated)
